source.author: verg
source.text: Dum iuga montis aper, fluvios dum piscis amabit, dumque thymo pascentur apes, dum rore cicadae, semper honos nomenque tuum laudesque manebunt; ut Baccho Cererique, tibi sic vota quotannis agricolae facient: damnabis tu quoque votis.
source.text_original: Dum iuga montis aper, fluvios dum piscis amabit, / dumque thymo pascentur apes, dum rore cicadae, / semper honos nomenque tuum laudesque manebunt; / ut Baccho Cererique, tibi sic vota quotannis / agricolae facient: damnabis tu quoque votis.
source.text_english: As long as the boar shall love the slopes of the mountain, the fish the rivers, and the bees feed on thyme, the cicadas on dew, your honor, your name, and your praises shall always endure; as to Bacchus and Ceres, so to you too each year the farmers will make their vows: you too will approve of vows.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Et in alio loco: In freta dum fluvii current, dum montibus umbrae Lustrabunt, convexa polus dum sidera pascet, Semper honos nomenque tuum laudesque manebunt.
reuse.text_original: Et in alio loco: In freta dum fluvii current, dum montibus umbrae Lustrabunt, convexa polus dum sidera pascet, Semper honos nomenque tuum laudesque manebunt.
reuse.text_english: And in another place: While rivers will run into the sea, while shadows will range over the mountains, while the sky will feed on the curved stars, your honor and name and praises shall always remain.
